# Writing With This Template {#sec-chapter1}

This chapter and @sec-chapter2 document the template itself. Replace both
with your own chapters once you have the hang of it; nothing here is
load-bearing.

## Where things go

`_quarto.yml` is the table of contents. The `chapters:` list controls both
the order of the book and which files are rendered at all --- a `.qmd` that
is not listed is ignored:

``` yaml
chapters:
  - index.qmd          # front matter: preface, dedication
  - intro.qmd
  - part: part-one.qmd # a part divider page
    chapters:
      - chapter1.qmd
      - chapter2.qmd
  - references.qmd
appendices:
  - appendix.qmd       # lettered separately from the main matter
```

A `part:` entry takes its own `.qmd` file, whose body becomes the text on
the divider page. Appendices go in the separate `appendices:` list so that
Quarto numbers them A, B, C rather than continuing the chapter count.

`index.qmd` is the front matter. It holds the preface, an optional
dedication page (commented out at the top of the file --- delete the
wrapper to enable it), and the `\mainmatter` switch that turns roman page
numbering into arabic. Anything above that switch is front matter and stays
unnumbered.

## Cross-references

Every referenceable thing takes an identifier prefixed by its type, and
`@id` inserts both the label and its number:

| Prefix | Refers to | Example |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `sec-` | Chapters and sections | `@sec-intro` |
| `eq-`  | Display equations | `@eq-linear` |
| `fig-` | Figures | `@fig-example` |
| `tbl-` | Tables | `@tbl-summary` |
| `thm-` | Theorems (and `lem-`, `cor-`, `def-`, `exm-`, `exr-`) | `@thm-ols` |

**Do not write the word "Section" in front of a `@sec-` reference.** Quarto
supplies the prefix, so `Section @sec-intro` renders as "Section Section
1". Write `@sec-intro` and let it produce "Section 1". The same applies to
`@fig-`, `@tbl-` and `@thm-`: never "Table @tbl-summary", just
`@tbl-summary`.

To write a reference in a sentence that needs a lower-case word, use
`-@sec-intro`, which prints the bare number.

## Equations

A display equation takes a label after the closing `$$`:

$$
y = X\beta + \varepsilon
$$ {#eq-linear}

and @eq-linear then refers to it. Drop the `{#eq-...}` and the equation
renders unnumbered. The template sets the space above a display equal to
the space below it (33.6pt each at this font size); the four LaTeX display
skips and the stray interline glue above a display are both handled in the
`include-in-header` block of `_quarto.yml`, so you should not need
`\vspace` around an equation.

Multi-line displays go in an `aligned` block:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hat{\beta} &= (X'X)^{-1}X'y \\
\hat{\sigma}^2 &= \frac{1}{n-k}\, \hat{\varepsilon}'\hat{\varepsilon}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ols}

## Theorems and proofs

Theorem environments are fenced divs whose identifier sets the kind. A
`##` heading inside the div becomes the parenthesised name:

::: {#thm-gauss}
## Gauss--Markov

Under the classical assumptions, the OLS estimator in @eq-ols is the best
linear unbiased estimator of $\beta$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Left to the reader, as is traditional.
:::

`#thm-` gives Theorem, and `#lem-`, `#cor-`, `#def-`, `#exm-` and `#exr-`
give Lemma, Corollary, Definition, Example and Exercise. Each counts
within its own chapter. `::: {.proof}` is unnumbered and ends with the
usual box; `.remark` and `.solution` work the same way.

## Callouts

::: {.callout-note}
Callouts come in five flavours: note, warning, tip, important and caution.
They render as framed asides in the PDF and as coloured boxes in HTML.
:::

## Citations

Citations resolve against `references.bib`. `@example2025` produces an
in-text citation --- @example2025 --- and `[@example2025]` a parenthetical
one [@example2025]. The bibliography is emitted wherever `references.qmd`
sits in the `chapters:` list.

This book uses Quarto's default citation processor, so a journal or
publisher style is a one-line change: add `csl: your-style.csl` next to
`bibliography:` in `_quarto.yml`.
